advances: A dimension-neutral slicing principle proves the requested bound for a coupled class: the budget can involve arbitrarily many binary coordinates and one unrestricted nonlinear coordinate, with arbitrarily many further unrestricted nonlinear coordinates absent from the budget. There is no restriction on retained mass fraction, coefficients, or factor laws. More generally, fixing k coordinates costs only the number N of nonempty slices; if at most one budget coefficient remains active, the bound is e^(-150) W/(N 2^(n-k)). The explicit consumer is the one-cut subgoal whenever N is at most 2^k. Binary sliced coordinates give an exact decomposition of the integral score.
author: research-agent
proof:
The product of the given global log-concave extensions, multiplied by the indicator of the closed halfspace \(\mathbf a\cdot x\le b\), is a finite-valued log-concave extension agreeing with every entry of w, including zeros. When both endpoint values are positive, the endpoints and their connecting segment lie in the halfspace, and the product log-concavity inequality applies. When an endpoint value is zero, the required lower bound is zero. Thus accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc` applies.

First prove inheritance from a coordinate slice, without restricting the budget coefficients. Fix \(s\in\Sigma\). Fixing these real coordinates in the extension gives a global log-concave extension of \(v_s\). Put \(D_s=\{y:v_s(y)>0\}\), \(v_{s,\max}=\max_{D_s}v_s\), and \(\phi^s_y=\log(v_{s,\max}/v_s(y))\). These are the canonical support, maximum weight, and potential of the slice. The exact normalization map is
\(\phi_{(s,y)}=\phi^s_y+\log(w_{\max}/v_{s,\max})\).

The affine injection \(y\mapsto(s,y)\) preserves affine independence, positive barycentric coefficients, and relative-interior barycenters. Every support in the slice family \(\mathcal E_j\) therefore embeds as a support in the ambient family \(\mathcal E_{(s,j)}\), with identical coefficients. The added constant in the potential cancels from its gap, so the two values of \(G_E\) agree. Here the families and gaps for each table have exactly the definitions of `488f0a583886b5fc`.

If F is an ambient integral hitting set at center \((s,j)\) and cutoff L, its intersection with this slice hits every slice support of gap at most L. Consequently \(\sum_{\mathbf I\in F}w_{\mathbf I}\ge\sum_{(s,y)\in F}v_s(y)\ge m_{\log}(j,L;v_s)\). Minimizing over F, then optimizing over j and L, proves \(\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\ge\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(v_s)\). This uses no fractional packing and changes no original weights.

If each factor indexed by T has at most two positive support points, each possible value \(s_i\) is an extremum of coordinate i over D. In a positive barycentric representation of \((s,j)\), the average of coordinate i equals this extremum, so every source has coordinate i equal to \(s_i\). Applying this to every \(i\in T\) forces every ambient barycentric support at \((s,j)\) to lie in this slice. The two support families thus coincide under the injection, with identical gaps and weights. An optimal slice hitting set is also an ambient hitting set, giving the reverse inequality of hitting masses. Every ambient center lies in one slice; optimization proves the exact score identity.

Now assume at most one coefficient outside T is active. For \(s\in\Sigma\), put \(c_s=\prod_{i\in T}u_i(s_i)>0\) and \(b_s=b-\sum_{i\in T}a_i s_i\), interpreting the empty product as one. If q is the unique active coordinate in R, then

\[
v_s(y)=c_s\left(u_q(y_q)\mathbf1_{\{a_qy_q\le b_s\}}\right)
\prod_{i\in R\setminus\{q\}}u_i(y_i).
\]

The truncated q-th factor is globally extendable and log-concave: multiply its given extension by the halfline indicator and use the direct log-concavity check above. It is nonzero because \(s\in\Sigma\). The other factors are unchanged. If no coefficient outside T is active, nonemptiness implies \(b_s\ge0\), and \(v_s(y)=c_s\prod_{i\in R}u_i(y_i)\). In either case absorb \(c_s\) into one factor, possible since \(r\ge1\). The slice satisfies every hypothesis of accepted product theorem `11cb4cde5378cfcd` in dimension r, with its original total mass \(W_s=\sum_yv_s(y)>0\). Hence \(\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(v_s)\ge e^{-150}2^{-r}W_s\).

The N slices partition D, so \(\sum_{s\in\Sigma}W_s=W\) and some slice has \(W_s\ge W/N\). Inheritance at that slice proves the displayed bound. If \(N\le2^k\), then \(N2^r\le2^n\). Binary sliced coordinates admit at most \(2^k\) assignments regardless of factor probabilities or which assignments the budget retains, proving the stated coupled class with no lower bound on retained fraction.
statement:
Let n be a positive integer, let u_i be nonzero, nonnegative, finitely supported, globally extendable log-concave tables on the integers, and let \(w_{\mathbf I}=\prod_{i=1}^n u_i(I_i)\mathbf1_{\{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf I\le b\}}\), where \(\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(W=\sum_{\mathbf I}w_{\mathbf I}>0\). Use precisely \(D\), \(\phi\), \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\), \(G_E\), \(m_{\log}\), and \(\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}\) from accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc`. Hitting costs always use integral sets and original weights.

Choose a proper coordinate subset \(T\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), put \(k=|T|\), and let \(R=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus T\) and \(r=n-k\ge1\). Suppose at most one \(i\in R\) has \(a_i\ne0\). Define \(\Sigma=\{\mathbf I_T:\mathbf I\in D\}\), \(N=|\Sigma|\), and \(v_s(y)=w_{(s,y)}\) for \(s\in\Sigma\), \(y\in\mathbb Z^R\), placing the coordinates in their original positions. Then

\[
\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)
\ge\max_{s\in\Sigma}\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(v_s)
\ge\frac{e^{-150}}{N\,2^{n-k}}W.
\]

Consequently \(N\le2^k\) implies \(\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\ge e^{-150}2^{-n}W\).

In particular the conclusion holds if every budget-active coordinate except at most one has positive-support cardinality at most two. Take T to consist of those binary budget-active coordinates, leaving a coordinate outside T if otherwise T would be all coordinates. Coordinates absent from the budget have no support-size or nonlinearity restriction. For a choice of T in which every factor indexed by T has at most two positive support points, the first displayed inequality is an equality. In fact, for every \(s\in\Sigma\), \(j\in\{y:v_s(y)>0\}\), and \(L\ge0\),
\(m_{\log}((s,j),L;w)=m_{\log}(j,L;v_s)\).

The quantitative input is accepted product theorem `11cb4cde5378cfcd`, applied once in dimension r to a retained slice. No claim is made for one-cut tables lacking a subset T satisfying the hypotheses and the slice-count bound.
